slides.0.title: Industry, markets and Diploma essays
slides.0.subtitle: Using numbers and structure to answer "why is Chilean wine the way it is?"
slides.1.title: The 2024 numbers
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Production fell
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Vinetur (13 June 2025): 2024 production fell 15.6% to just over 930 million litres
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Exports rose
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Exports of 780 million litres (+14.4%) worth about US$1.73 billion (+6.1%); bottled wine was 54% of volume and 75% of value
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Market shifts
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Brazil was the largest bottled market (about +30%); China's bottled volume fell 11.5%; the domestic market is about US$3.8 billion
slides.1.content: Lower output with higher exports points to destocking and export orientation, not a demand surge.
slides.2.title: Structure: concentration and export focus
slides.2.highlights.0.title: The top ten
slides.2.highlights.0.content: Portal Fruticola (September 2012): in January to July 2012 the top ten wineries took 53% of bottled export value (US$786.3 million), about US$416.6 million
slides.2.highlights.1.title: The leaders
slides.2.highlights.1.content: In order then: Concha y Toro (US$151.6 million), Cono Sur (same group, US$53.3 million), San Pedro (CCU, US$48.7 million), Santa Rita (US$29.1 million)
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Mind the date
slides.2.highlights.2.content: These are 2012 data and not directly comparable with 2024 figures; date them in an essay and supplement with current statistics
slides.2.content: A few large groups carry exports, so brands and price tiers are highly concentrated.
slides.3.title: Blind-tasting clues
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Reds
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Ripe black fruit with jalapeño, bell pepper and black pepper suggests Carmenère; for Cabernet, weigh Maipo structure against ripeness elsewhere
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Whites
slides.3.highlights.1.content: High acidity and saline minerality point to cool coasts (Casablanca, Leyda, Limarí), against rounder fruit from warmer inland sites
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Old-vine styles
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Old-vine País, Cinsault and Carignan: light body, red fruit and fine tannin point to Itata or Maule
slides.3.content: Read climate and ripeness first, narrow to grape and region, and only then judge quality and price.
slides.4.title: An essay template
slides.4.highlights.0.title: Claim
slides.4.highlights.0.content: Answer the question in one sentence, e.g. "Chile's advantage is stable climate and own-rooted vines, but water is its biggest structural risk"
slides.4.highlights.1.title: Evidence
slides.4.highlights.1.content: Pair every point with a sourced, dated figure or event, e.g. 280 mm rainfall, the 2010 earthquake, 2024 exports
slides.4.highlights.2.title: Caveat and conclusion
slides.4.highlights.2.content: Flag disputed or dated sources, return to the claim and state the implication for regions, brands or consumers
slides.4.content: The MW style prizes a view, evidence, and an admission of uncertainty.
Per Vinetur, Chile's 2024 wine production changed by?
Bottled wine was about what share of 2024 export value?
Which country was the largest bottled-wine market in 2024?
Up about 30%; China's bottled volume fell 11.5%.
In January to July 2012, the top ten wineries held what share of bottled export value?
Cono Sur belongs to the same group as which winery?
In the essay template, what should you do with dated data?
A. State the year and supplement with current statistics
Admitting uncertainty is part of the MW style.
